transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-23
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood CSM), Aisha Raman (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (SilverHarbor Head of MLOps), Daniel Kim (SilverHarbor Cloud Architect), Priya Nair (SilverHarbor PM)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
- Handoff of the onboarding runbook and staging plan; discussed VPC peering, SSO, RBAC and observability requirements.
- Agreed to schedule network window for peering test and for Redwood to provision staging credentials.
- Action items assigned for runbook delivery, token provisioning, and internal stakeholder confirmation.

Topics: runbook walk-through; network connectivity; identity and access; staging -> prod cutover plan; monitoring & alerts; pilot metrics

Transcript:
00:00 - Michael Chen: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for taking time. I'm Mike from Redwood, I'm the CSM on this account, and we'll do a quick onramp and runbook handoff. How's everybody doing?
00:12 - Ellen Park: Hi Mike, doing well, thanks. We've got the core folks here, Daniel and Priya, we'll jump in.
00:18 - Daniel Kim: Hey, yeah morning for me, afternoon for you. Lots to go through so yeah let's get started.
00:28 - Aisha Raman: Thanks all, I'm Aisha on the SE side. I'll be driving the staging setup and the network tests with Daniel.
00:35 - Priya Nair: Hi! Priya here, I'll be tracking pilot success criteria and product integration notes.
00:44 - Michael Chen: Great. Quick agenda: I'll run through the onboarding runbook, Aisha will talk technical steps for staging and peering, then we'll cover SSO and roles, monitoring, and finish with next steps. Any additions?
00:56 - Ellen Park: Maybe just add the data retention and audit log questions up front — security team flagged those.
01:02 - Michael Chen: Good call. We'll touch that with the logging section.

01:20 - Michael Chen: Okay, so runbook high level: three phases — staging verification, pilot (limited traffic), and production cutover. Staging is usually 1-2 weeks, runs on Redwood Dedicated or hosted? quick question, which are you targeting?
01:35 - Ellen Park: We want private deployment ideally, we need VPC peering and KMS integration, but for speed of experiment we can use hosted with strict data retention while we evaluate.
01:48 - Michael Chen: Understood. Hosted to start then migrate to Private; we can enable KMS on Private, for hosted we have customer-managed keys via the KMS integration? small note: hosted has an option for bring-your-own-kms but there are some limitations.
02:05 - Daniel Kim: Can you clarify that? We assumed KMS would be supported the same for both. Our security asks for end-to-end key control.
02:14 - Aisha Raman: Short answer: full KMS/HSM integration is available in Redwood Private. Hosted supports envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for certain flows, but not HSM-backed key rotation the same way — the runbook section 3.2 clarifies. We'll share the doc.
02:32 - Priya Nair: Okay that's fine for now, we'll start hosted but we need to lock a migration path to private.

02:45 - Michael Chen: Good. Network and peering: Aisha, can you walk the steps?
02:50 - Aisha Raman: Sure. Step one: we need an egress IP list from Redwood for the staging pool. We'll provide a CIDR and a set of origin IPs; Daniel will create a peering and firewall rule. Then we'll validate with curl tests to the staging endpoint, and finally run a small token-based throughput test.
03:10 - Daniel Kim: The tricky bit for us is our egress is NAT'd through a set of firewalls and we have strict outbound rules. We'll need the peering to be inbound initiated by our side and not require open egress rules.
03:22 - Aisha Raman: Yep, we have a port and protocol list in the runbook. Also note Redwood uses both TCP 443 and websocket for streaming, so WebSocket traffic needs to be allowed.
03:36 - Ellen Park: Websockets are a problem for our older edge devices — any workaround?
03:41 - Aisha Raman: You can fall back to chunked HTTPS streaming if websockets are blocked; performance differs, but it's supported. I'll mark that in the runbook as an alternative.

04:05 - Michael Chen: On observability — console dashboards, token-level cost metrics, and per-route latency traces are all available. For the pilot we recommend instrumenting three metrics: 99th pct latency, token cost per response, and error rate. Priya, is that aligned with your product goals?
04:27 - Priya Nair: Yes, 99p latency and error rate are core, and we'll add a quality metric — human eval of 50 prompt/responses during pilot. We want regression alerts if quality drops more than 5%.
04:38 - Michael Chen: Great, Redwood Optimize can auto-suggest batching and quantization for cost targets, but we'll keep the pilot on default to measure baseline. After two weeks, SE will run optimization suggestions.

05:03 - Daniel Kim: A practical question: what's the token billing cadence for the staging pool and can we isolate spend by environment?
05:10 - Michael Chen: Yes, we support environment-level tagging and cost breakdowns; tokens consumed in staging will be tag-scoped and show separately in the console. Billing remains monthly but we can export CSVs for accounting.

05:24 - Aisha Raman: Ok onto SSO and RBAC: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Role templates: Admin, Dev, Read-only, and Ops. You can map groups from your IdP. Any special roles you need?
05:39 - Ellen Park: We need a role for 'ML Evaluations' team with access to logs and evals but not billing. Can that be scoped?
05:47 - Aisha Raman: Yes, we can create a custom RBAC role and tie it to your group via SCIM. We'll add that to the runbook steps.

06:05 - Michael Chen: Security / compliance quick notes: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs; audit logs can be exported for 12 months on hosted, indefinite on private. Also there is an audit events webhook if you want streaming audit logs.
06:20 - Daniel Kim: The security team will want the SOC 2 report and a quick run through of audit webhook SLA. Can you send the compliance pack?
06:27 - Michael Chen: Yes, I'll attach the security pack after the call.

06:35 - Ellen Park: Question on model versioning and rollouts: we plan to test two model families for reranking and generation; how do we canary?
06:45 - Aisha Raman: Redwood Console supports canary traffic splits and automatic fallback to a lower cost model on errors. You can set per-route rollout rules. We'll add a canary template to the runbook.
06:58 - Priya Nair: Nice. For the pilot we'll do 10% traffic to new model, monitor quality.
07:05 - Michael Chen: Sounds good. A note about KV cache and latency — if you plan long context with retrieval augmented generation, we recommend dedicated pools with large GPU memory. That affects cost, we'll flag recommended instance types.
07:22 - Daniel Kim: We'll probably run the retriever in our infra and call Redwood for the generation path. Is that a common pattern?
07:29 - Aisha Raman: Very common. Keep your retrieval and prefiltering upstream, Redwood does the heavy token work. That reduces token spend and latency for repeated patterns via prefix caching.

07:50 - Michael Chen: Ok, timeline and pilot metrics: proposed 2 weeks staging validation, 3 week pilot, then production cutover window. Does that align with your internal calendar?
08:02 - Priya Nair: We can try to start staging next week, but need Daniel to confirm peering window.
08:09 - Daniel Kim: I can do peering next Tuesday, need the egress IP list two days prior to update firewall rules.
08:16 - Michael Chen: We'll send egress IP list by Friday EOD.

08:25 - Ellen Park: One more question — backups and data retention. For hosted pilot, we need logs to be deleted after 30 days for now. Can that be configured?
08:33 - Aisha Raman: Yes, retention policy per project can be set in the console; 30-day retention is supported for hosted. We'll include config steps.

08:45 - Michael Chen: All right let's recap next steps quickly. I'll read out what's on my list.
08:51 - Michael Chen: Michael to send runbook PDF, compliance pack, and egress IP list by Friday (that's 2027-05-24). Aisha to provision staging API keys and put the sample prompt set in the shared drive by 05-25. Daniel to provide VPC peering diagram and firewall contacts by 05-28 and schedule the network window next Tuesday. Priya to confirm pilot success criteria and stakeholder list by 05-27.
09:18 - Priya Nair: That sounds right to me.
09:21 - Daniel Kim: Yup, we'll get the diagrams out.
09:24 - Ellen Park: Thanks team. Appreciate the clarity, especially on KMS vs private.
09:30 - Aisha Raman: Quick note — if websockets are blocked during the peering test, we'll run chunked HTTPS test and document performance delta.
09:42 - Michael Chen: Perfect. Any final questions?
09:47 - Priya Nair: One last thing — can Redwood share a short checklist for our QA team to validate response quality?
09:53 - Aisha Raman: Yes, we'll add a 10-point QA checklist to the runbook and include the 50-sample prompts Priya mentioned.
10:01 - Michael Chen: Great. If nothing else we'll wrap. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with documents and an invite for the peering window.
10:10 - Ellen Park: Thanks all.
10:12 - Daniel Kim: Thanks, bye.
10:14 - Priya Nair: Bye.

Notes on transcript fidelity: speakers sometimes overlap and the auto-timed timestamps are approximate. Some Redwood product names auto-transcribed oddly (e.g., "Redwood Dedicted" instead of "Redwood Dedicated").

Referenced artifacts / links: runbook (link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/silverharbor-onramp), compliance pack (link: https://redwood.example/security/socs/silverharbor-pack), shared drive folder (link: https://drive.example.com/silverharbor-pilot)
